components.css: .ds-topbar { display: flex; align-items: stretch; gap: 32px; height: 56px; padding: 0 24px; background: rgb(11 11 16 / 0.94); border-top: 3px solid var(--red, #e10600); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #2b2b3a); font-family: var(--font, "Titillium Web", system-ui, sans-serif); color: var(--text, #f4f4f7); } .ds-wordmark { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 900; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-size: 1.2rem; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-wordmark span { color: var(--red-hi, #ff2a1f); } .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: stretch; gap: 2px; } .ds-nav a { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 20px; margin: 10px 0; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--muted, #a2a2b6); clip-path: polygon(var(--slant, 10px) 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - var(--slant, 10px)) 100%, 0 100%); transition: background-color var(--fast, 160ms) var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)), color var(--fast, 160ms) var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)); } .ds-nav a:hover { color: var(--text, #f4f4f7); background: var(--panel-2, #1b1b26); } .ds-nav a[aria-current="page"] { background: var(--red, #e10600); color: #fff; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--text, #f4f4f7); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-soon { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 0 16px; color: var(--muted, #a2a2b6); font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; white-space: nowrap; cursor: default; } .ds-soon small { border: 1px solid var(--faint, #8b8ba1); padding: 0 6px; font-size: 0.65rem; letter-spacing: 0.12em; line-height: 1.5; }

components.css: .ds-strip { display: flex; align-items: stretch; font-family: var(--font, "Titillium Web", system-ui, sans-serif); filter: drop-shadow(0 10px 24px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45)); } .ds-strip-tag { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 22px 0 18px; margin-right: -10px; position: relative; z-index: 1; background: var(--red, #e10600); color: #fff; font-weight: 700; font-style: italic; text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 1.1rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 14px) 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-strip-title { display: flex; align-items: center; min-height: 64px; padding: 6px 40px 6px 30px; background: var(--white-strip, #f4f4f7); color: var(--ink, #0b0b10); clip-path: polygon(14px 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 14px) 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-strip-title h1 { margin: 0; line-height: 1.1; font-size: clamp(1.6rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem); font-style: italic; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.005em; } .ds-strip-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 18px; padding: 6px 30px; margin-left: -12px; background: var(--panel-2, #1b1b26); color: var(--muted, #a2a2b6); font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-size: 0.85rem; clip-path: polygon(14px 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 14px) 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-strip-meta b { color: var(--text, #f4f4f7); font-weight: 700; }

components.css: .ds-tower { display: grid; gap: 2px; font-family: var(--font, "Titillium Web", system-ui, sans-serif); color: var(--text, #f4f4f7); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 40px 5px 52px minmax(0, 1fr) auto; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 34px; padding-right: 12px; background: var(--panel, #13131b); transition: background-color 160ms; } .ds-row:hover { background: var(--panel-2, #1b1b26); } .ds-pos { align-self: stretch; display: grid; place-items: center; background: var(--panel-3, #242432); font-weight: 900; } .ds-leader .ds-pos { background: var(--white-strip, #f4f4f7); color: var(--ink, #0b0b10); } .ds-team { align-self: stretch; margin: 6px 0; background: var(--team, #8b8ba1); } .ds-code { font-weight: 700; font-style: italic; font-size: 1.05rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-name { color: var(--muted, #a2a2b6); font-size: 0.85rem; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-val { font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; text-align: right; }

components.css: .ds-lights { display: flex; gap: 10px; } .ds-lights span { display: grid; gap: 5px; padding: 6px 5px; background: #08080b; border: 1px solid var(--line, #2b2b3a); } .ds-lights i { width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: #2a0b0b; animation: ds-light 3.2s infinite; } .ds-lights span:nth-child(2) i { animation-delay: 0.3s; } .ds-lights span:nth-child(3) i { animation-delay: 0.6s; } .ds-lights span:nth-child(4) i { animation-delay: 0.9s; } .ds-lights span:nth-child(5) i { animation-delay: 1.2s; } @keyframes ds-light { 0%, 6% { background: #2a0b0b; } 10%, 78% { background: var(--red-hi, #ff2a1f); } 82%, 100% { background: #2a0b0b; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-lights i { animation: none; } }

narrative.northStar: The Flight Hardware Showcase (AeroLabs AI company page, /) and The Broadcast Graphics Package (F1 Data Hub, /f1)
narrative.overview:
This file holds two visual worlds. The route decides which one applies; the app sets `body[data-section]` from the route table and every world-specific rule hangs off that attribute.

F1 Data Hub (/f1): Every screen reads like the on-air graphics of a race broadcast. Data arrives as timing-tower strips, lower-third title bars and a circuit map, never as dashboard cards. The ground is carbon black, panels sit one cool step above it, and the data itself is white. Broadcast red is a signal colour, not a theme colour: it marks selection, live state and the active tab.

The form language is the slanted strip. Titles, tabs, buttons, segmented controls, the countdown and the weather band are four-point parallelograms cut with clip-path, butted together with 2px seams the way a broadcast tower stacks its rows. Titillium Web carries everything: heavy italic uppercase for titles and three-letter driver codes, upright tabular figures for times, gaps and readouts. Density is high and deliberate, like a TV graphic built to be read in a glance.

Motion serves live data: tower rows slide to new positions, car markers glide between refreshes, the fastest lap draws itself around the circuit, and five start lights stand in for a spinner during slow loads. All of it is cancelled under reduced motion.

The package sits under the Aerolabs AI brand: F1 Data Hub is its F1 section, named in the first nav tab, and the top bar carries the AeroLabs AI logo mark beside the text wordmark. In the Persuade register (the landing page) the package runs at full coverage: a real fastest lap replays across a full-bleed hero as the only image, HUD readouts and a podium tower are read off it like an onboard graphic, and three oversized slanted tabs carry the ways in.

AeroLabs AI company page (/): The company page is an aerospace-corporate showcase, built in the register of a space-industry company site (EnduroSat was the user's style reference; none of its assets or copy are used). Pure black ground, monumental centred uppercase type, and products presented like flight hardware: a name, a status, large spec figures with small tracked labels, and a real visual beside them. Nothing is decorative. The only imagery is real product output: the latest race's fastest lap replaying under the hero, and the latest classification beside F1 Data Hub; ASTRAEUS, not yet built, gets a plain orbital context diagram.

Archivo carries the world, bold (700) to extra-bold (800) uppercase with tight negative tracking for the headline, product names and closing line; regular weight for copy and the vision statement; 600-weight tracked uppercase for labels and statuses. Structure is hairlines on black: 1px dark-grey rules divide every band and every row; there are no cards, panels or shadows. Density is low and the page is long, centred where it states and two-column where it shows a product.

One accent: the AeroLabs logo cyan. On `/` it is the primary action, the live state, inline action links, focus and selection, and the "AI" in the wordmark. Everything else is white, cool grey and black.

rules.name: The Route Decides The World Rule
rules.body: A surface takes exactly one world, chosen by its route. New pages under `/f1` are broadcast pages; new company pages sit outside `/f1` and take the showcase world. Slanted strips, Titillium Web, the carbon panel steps and broadcast red as a UI signal never appear on `/`; Archivo, the pure-black showcase palette and logo cyan as a UI colour never appear under `/f1`.

rules.name: The Signal Red Rule
rules.body: Red means selected, live or leading. It never decorates a surface that carries no state.

rules.name: The Letter With The Colour Rule
rules.body: Team colour appears only as a thin sliver beside a driver code; compound colour only with its letter. Position numbers and codes carry the meaning; colour reinforces it.

rules.name: The Line Is The Image Rule
rules.body: On the landing hero the speed-coloured racing line is the only picture: no photography, screenshots or illustration behind the overlays.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: On `/`, logo cyan is the only colour that is not black, white or grey, and it marks action or live state (plus focus and selection). It never fills a surface, a heading or a decorative shape. In the F1 world logo cyan stays inside the logo mark only.

rules.name: The Real Output Rule
rules.body: On `/` the only pictures are real product output (the live lap, the live classification) or a plain hairline diagram for a product not yet built. No photography, renders, illustration, gradients or glows.

rules.name: The Words With The Mark Rule
rules.body: Status is shape and words together: a solid cyan dot with "Live now" in white for a live product; a dashed grey ring with "Under construction" in grey for one not yet built.

rules.name: The Two Postures Rule
rules.body: Names lean, numbers stand. Driver codes, titles and Grand Prix names are italic; times, gaps, positions and readouts are upright and tabular.

rules.name: The Figure Over Label Rule
rules.body: Every number on `/` is large, upright and tabular, with a small grey 600 tracked-uppercase label beneath it naming what it measures. Labels name data; they never sit above a heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces by panel step and 2px seams. No glass, no blur, no card shadows.

rules.name: The Hairline Only Rule
rules.body: Separation on `/` is a 1px hairline-grey rule or nothing. No cards, panels, fills, shadows or glows to group content.

dos: **Do** cut every tab, button, segment and title segment as a four-point parallelogram (10px slant on controls, 14px on strips).
**Do** stack rows with 2px seams on panel instead of borders or separate cards.
**Do** keep broadcast red for selected, live and leading states.
**Do** set driver codes and names in italic 700 uppercase, and all times, gaps and positions upright with tabular figures.
**Do** pair every team colour with a driver code and every compound colour with its letter.
**Do** use an inset 2px data-white ring for focus on clipped shapes.
**Do** explain missing data in a dashed state block rather than showing a raw error.
**Do** give the landing's ways in as 72px slanted CTA tabs (16px slant), with only the primary action in broadcast red.
**Do** replay hero laps as a ghost lap: the full lap at 32% opacity, live segments at full strength behind the car.
**Do** resolve the world from the route: `data-section="aerolabs"` on `/` only, `data-section="f1"` on `/f1` and every `/f1/*` route, with the `--al-*` tokens declared only under the aerolabs scope.
**Do** keep logo cyan on `/` to the primary action, the live state, inline action links, focus and selection, and the wordmark's "AI".
**Do** present each product like flight hardware: name, status mark with words, large tabular figures over small tracked uppercase labels, and a real visual with a caption.
**Do** take every figure on `/` from the live API, showing "--" or a plain unavailable line rather than an invented number.
**Do** separate bands and rows with 1px hairline-grey rules on pure black.
**Do** set the hero statement in Archivo 700 uppercase with tight negative tracking, centred, and product names and the closing line at 800.
**Do** show the completed lap, still, under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use rounded rectangles; circles are only for tyres, lights, car markers and the live dot.
**Don't** use glass, blur or gradients on text. Gradients appear only as the speed-scale legend, the loading shimmer and the landing hero's bottom legibility scrim.
**Don't** build KPI tiles or rounded card grids; data goes into towers, strips and the circuit map.
**Don't** use the F1 logo, official Formula 1 typefaces or trademarked marks.
**Don't** let a motion run when reduced motion is requested.
**Don't** carry slanted strips, Titillium Web, the carbon panel steps or broadcast red as a UI signal onto `/`, or Archivo, the showcase palette and logo cyan as a UI colour into `/f1`.
**Don't** use gradients, glass, glows, shadows, rounded corners, cards or panel fills on `/`.
**Don't** put photography, renders or illustration on `/`; the pictures are real product output or a plain hairline diagram.
**Don't** use a second accent colour on `/`; team and speed colours appear only inside F1 Data Hub's own data graphics.
**Don't** invent specs, partners or dates for a product that is not built; label its visual a concept.
